data.narrative:
Astera Labs is a publicly traded semiconductor company founded by Jitendra Mohan, Sanjay Gajendra, and Casey Morrison. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four same-sector, same-stage public comparables: Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B).

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The median valuation across these four Chips & Semiconductors public companies is $19.0B, with valuations ranging from $1.1B at the low end to $39.2B at the high end. A public-comp anchoring approach using price-to-sales multiples (21.5x median across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which are typically unavailable for private-stage targets and do not constrain this analysis.

The triangulated valuation range supports a median estimate of $19.0B, with a low-end bound of $16.2B and high-end of $21.9B. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single applicable method and the wide dispersion within the peer set itself—a $38B spread from minimum to maximum—indicating material uncertainty around valuation within the semiconductor sector. Key uncertainties include market comparability given the heterogeneity of chip-subsector focus and commercialization stage across peers, as well as the absence of revenue or profitability data to calibrate relative positioning.
